    • findOptionalByUsername

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public Optional<PUser> findOptionalByUsername(String username)
      Looks a user up by name without hiding deactivated accounts, unlike findUserByUsername(java.lang.String). Used where the caller has to see that a name is occupied rather than whether the account is usable.

    • updateUser

      @Transactional public PUser updateUser(PUser user)
      Full update of a user's editable profile (PUT semantics). Replaces the profile fields the request owns, but deliberately preserves the credential and authorization state — password, roles, personal permissions and the department — which never travel through this endpoint and are managed by dedicated, elevated-authorization operations. This is applied onto the managed entity loaded from the database rather than by saving the detached request shell: saving the shell would have persisted its empty/null password, roles and permissions over the stored ones, silently wiping the user's credentials and role assignments on an ordinary profile edit.

    • getRoleIds

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public Set<Long> getRoleIds(Long userId)
      Returns the ids of the roles currently assigned to the user. Because PUser.roles is a lazy collection, this must be read inside a transaction — the caller (e.g. the admin role selector in the user form) uses the ids to pre-select role items loaded separately, rather than touching the lazy association off a detached entity.

    • setRoles

      @Transactional public PUser setRoles(Long userId, Set<Long> roleIds)
      Replaces the user's assigned roles with exactly the roles identified by roleIds (a full replace: roles not in the set are unassigned, new ones are added). This is the dedicated, elevated-authorization role-assignment operation deliberately excluded from partialUpdateUser(java.lang.Long, de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.model.security.PUser); like the rest of this admin-console service it carries no per-call authorization parameter and is gated by the admin login in front of the UI. user_roles is owned by PUser, so setting the managed collection and saving persists the join rows. A null or empty set clears all roles.
